content: The region in question does not have a fluoridated public water supply, and public dental care services for children in the specified age group are limited. Participants in the study were from families with an income of up to two Brazilian minimum wages, equivalent to approximately $208 per year. Children were eligible for the study if they were between 18 and 42 months old and had parental consent to participate. Children were categorized into two groups: those who were breastfed for less than 12 months (non-exposed group) and those who were still being breastfed at the time of examination (exposed group). Exclusion criteria included the presence of debilitating systemic diseases as reported by parents and the administration of antibiotics within the last 30 days, as this could interfere with the colonization of mutans streptococci. A validated questionnaire was administered to the mothers or guardians to collect demographic data, and a 24-hour food recall interview was conducted to assess dietary information. The questionnaire and clinical examination were performed on separate occasions to ensure that information on risk factors obtained from the questionnaire did not influence the clinical diagnosis of caries lesions. A single calibrated professional clinically evaluated carious lesions in the children. The decayed, missing, and filled teeth (dmft) scores were calculated for each child. A random 15% sample of household addresses was selected, and trained fieldworkers enumerated the residents at each selected household. All children aged 6 to 14 years were invited to participate in the study. Parents completed a questionnaire for each child under the supervision of a trained fieldworker. Data on breastfeeding duration were collected as a categorical variable, categorized as breastfed for less than 6 months, 6 to 12 months, or more than 12 months. Blinding of participants and personnel, as well as outcome assessment, was unclear in terms of risk of bias. Selective reporting and other biases were also judged to have unclear risk.
